chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who employs a worker, and the worker steals from his house. Would his hand be cut? He (peace be upon him) said: 'This one is a trustee, he is not a thief. This is treachery.'

key_terms.مُؤْتَمَنٌ: a trustee / one entrusted with property

ai.seo_question: Does an employee who steals from their employer's house have their hand cut off in Islamic law?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the legal category of 'theft' (sariqah) warranting hand amputation and 'breach of trust' (khiyanah) for an employee stealing from their employer's home. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the specific conditions for hudud punishments are strict, often classifying such acts as discretionary punishment (ta'zir) due to the pre-existing trust relationship. It underscores the ethical weight of amanah in employment contracts within Islamic law.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazaz, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who employed someone on wages, so he stole from his house. Would his hand be cut?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This one was a trustee, he is not with a theft. This is treachery’.
